title: Bargo

serverInfo.name: bargo-stocks
serverInfo.title: Bargo
serverInfo.description: Bargo MCP server: read-only access to a curated market dataset — relevance-scored financial news + AI sentiment, SEC Form 4 insider activity, Twitter-analyst sentiment, options flow, AI-compute pricing, and algo-distribution signals.

authentication.instructions: Get an MCP token from https://www.bargo.ai (sign in with an authorized Google account, then GET /api/mcp-token). Pass it as `Authorization: Bearer swmcp_...` or `X-Api-Key: swmcp_...`. The handshake and tools/list are open; the key is required for tool calls.

tools.name: get_comprehensive_snapshot
tools.description: PRIMARY market-read tool — call this FIRST for broad 'what's happening / full picture / market read' questions that need every structured lens. For explicit AI/stock/ticker/company news, headlines, articles, or current coverage use get_news_feed or get_trending_news. Do NOT use this as the first tool for source-evidence, Twitter/X discourse, authority-handle discussion, expert commentary, AI/agentic-AI debate, podcasts, transcripts, filings, or source-quote questions; use find_market_context first for those, even if the user says 'latest discussion'. Returns the complete latest snapshot from stored rows across EVERY pivot in ONE call: AI capital cycle; analyst-tweet sentiment & handle bias; market microstructure / algo distribution; options flow; valuations & top stocks; trending AI-stock news & sentiment; token / inference demand; GPU & CPU rental pricing; hyperscaler compute ownership & capex/spend; datacenter buildout (current + forward pipeline); demand-elasticity signals (demand pressure vs price softening); hedge-fund 13F holdings & insider (Form 4) buying; Polymarket; Korea exports; digests. Includes a `sourcesIncluded` list and a `freshness` map — synthesize across every lens and flag any stale ones. Use the granular tools only to drill into specifics afterward. Read-only; no LLM, no live fetchers.

tools.name: get_compute_economics
tools.description: AI-compute SUPPLY/DEMAND read in ONE call — the synthesized Compute Tightness Index (GPU rental-market tightness, the INPUT) paired with the Token Demand Index (inference consumption + effective price, the OUTPUT). Use for the AI capital-cycle / elasticity question: is GPU capacity tightening or loosening, and is token demand outrunning the falling per-token price? Returns `computeTightness`: 0–100 score (regime Loose/Balanced/Tight/Acute), 30-day delta + direction, per-GPU (B200/H200/H100) spot-vs-on-demand pricing + per-GPU CTI, and recent daily history; and `tokenDemand`: total tokens/week + demand index (100 = series start), 30-day and since-start % change, open-source share %, demand-weighted effective $/1M, implied weekly spend, per-provider-group breakdown, and history. These are the synthesized gauges; for the RAW underlying rows use get_spot_pricing (GPU rental) and get_inference_economics (token price + demand). Read-only.

tools.name: get_fund_holdings
tools.description: 13F institutional / hedge-fund holdings (SEC 13F-HR), one row per position per fund per quarter. Use this whenever asked what hedge funds or institutions OWN, HOLD, or are BUYING. Filter by `ticker` (which funds hold it), by `fund` (a fund's top positions, name or CIK), or pass neither for the most institutionally-held tickers. Without an explicit quarter, returns BOTH the current filing quarter and the latest broadly reported comparison quarter, with coverage for each.

tools.name: get_fund_letters
tools.description: Fund investor letters and memos (quarterly/monthly letters, commentaries, reports) scraped from ~800 fund managers' own sites — the catalog of the narrative WHY behind 13F position changes. Use to enumerate what a manager published and when: filter by `fund` (fund or manager name, e.g. 'Greenlight'), `quarter` (2025Q4), `doc_type`. Returns metadata only (no full text — the letters are copyrighted); to READ what a letter argues, search find_market_context with sourceKinds=['fund_letter'], which returns attributed excerpts.

tools.name: get_activist_letters
tools.description: Activist / proxy-fight campaign letters from SEC EDGAR (DFAN14A soliciting material, PREC14A/DEFC14A/PRRN14A dissident proxies, PX14A6G exempt solicitations, Schedule 13D EX-99 exhibit letters). `ticker` is the TARGET company under attack; the activist filer is in `activist`. Use when asked what an activist wrote/demanded, which companies are under activist pressure, or for a campaign's paper trail. These are public SEC records — `url` serves the full document (fetch via browse_url). Quote-level search across them: find_market_context sourceKinds=['activist_letter'].

tools.name: get_insider_trades
tools.description: SEC Form 4 insider transactions (officers / directors / 10% owners). Use when asked about insider buying/selling. txn_code: P = open-market BUY (the strongest signal), S = sale, A = grant, M = option exercise, F = tax withhold. Set `buysOnly` for open-market buys only. Filter by `ticker` or pass none for recent market-wide activity.

tools.name: get_podcast_coverage
tools.description: Podcast + newsletter coverage for a ticker or private company (OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX...): who is discussing it, how much vs. the prior-window baseline (a sudden burst on a quiet small cap is the promotion-screen primitive), recent SUBSTANTIVE quotes with click-to-listen links into the publisher's audio at the exact second, verified guest/exec appearances, and any pre-registered promotion flags. Every quote includes episodeId for immediate drill-down with get_podcast_episode. MUST-CALL when asked what podcasts/shows are saying about a name, for small caps and private companies with no sell-side coverage, and as evidence color in single-stock reads. Quotes are verbatim and verifiable: cite them WITH their listen link. Flags come from an append-only pre-registered record with NO outcomes graded until Jan 2027 — present them as evidence, never as a performance claim.

tools.name: get_promotion_screen
tools.description: The podcast promotion screen: small caps flagged for a sudden burst of podcast/newsletter coverage after a long quiet period — the footprint of manufactured attention (SEC 17(b) stock promotion). Returns the current flag list from a FROZEN, PRE-REGISTERED, APPEND-ONLY rule with per-flag evidence (venue concentration, exec appearances, sponsored language) and links into get_podcast_coverage for the quotes. MUST-CALL when asked which stocks look promoted/pumped, for short-candidate or avoid-list screening, and as a diligence check on any sudden small-cap mover. HARD PRESENTATION RULE: outcomes are NOT graded until Jan 2027 — always present flags as evidence a name is being heavily promoted, NEVER as a prediction, performance claim, or sell recommendation; say the rule is pre-registered and ungraded every time.

tools.name: get_podcast_episode
tools.description: The full-episode view for a podcast mention: the publisher's own audio URL (the mp3 IS the whole conversation — we never serve transcript text or rehost audio) plus a TIMELINE of every company discussed on the episode with the second it happens, verbatim excerpt, and salience, so a user can play the episode and jump between moments. Use after find_market_context or get_podcast_coverage when the user wants the whole conversation behind a quote: pass the episodeId from verify/quote rows. Present as: listen at the publisher link; timestamps are jump markers.

tools.name: get_table_catalog
tools.description: STRUCTURED DATA FALLBACK / schema discovery. Do NOT call this first for long-form evidence, expert commentary, filings/earnings reports, transcripts, podcasts, raw tweets, Twitter OCR/video transcripts, or source-quote questions; use find_market_context first for those. Use this only to discover structured tables when no dedicated tool fits, or when the user explicitly asks what tables exist. Auth, user-submission, and internal search-index tables are intentionally excluded.

tools.name: find_market_context
tools.description: PRIMARY evidence search — call this FIRST for raw/source-extracted market text, expert commentary, source quotes, SEC filings/earnings reports, earnings-call transcripts, podcast transcripts, raw tweets, Twitter media OCR/video transcripts, Substack posts, raw Truth Social posts, fund managers' investor letters (sourceKinds=['fund_letter']), and activist campaign letters (sourceKinds=['activist_letter'], ticker = target company). This is the right first tool for broad AI-discussion questions and authority-handle/Twitter questions, including: 'latest discussion on agentic AI', 'check the discussion on agentic AI', 'what are authority handles saying about AI agents?', 'Dylan Patel where the next AI buildout bottleneck shows up', 'SemiAnalysis CPO AAOI commentary', 'what are people saying about HBM supply?', 'show primary-source context on AI capex', or 'find long-form discussion of CoWoS'. For broad discourse, search sourceKinds like tweet, tweet_media_text, podcast_transcript, substack_post, transcript. Transcript results are stored body-text chunks, not pages to browse: call get_market_context_item (fullSource=true for the whole transcript) and treat their URL as provenance only. Do NOT start those with generic web/search, news tools, get_recent_tweets, get_table_catalog, get_table_rows, or query_readonly_sql. Do NOT use for structured numeric data such as prices, fundamentals, sell-side predictions, macro signals, algo flow, options/GEX, signed flow, correlations, or the earnings calendar; use dedicated tools for those.

tools.name: get_market_context_item
tools.description: Fetch stored body text for one find_market_context result, optionally with neighboring chunks or the complete source. Use this after search when the agent needs enough raw/source-extracted context to quote/summarize a filing, earnings-call transcript, podcast transcript, tweet media OCR/video transcript, raw tweet, or raw Truth Social post. For transcripts, use fullSource=true when the whole call is needed. For a PODCAST passage hit, fullSource=true returns the ENTIRE episode script (timestamped '[h:mm:ss] text' lines) when stored — page long episodes with scriptOffset=nextScriptOffset from the previous response. Chunked sources page with chunkStart=nextChunkStart. Never browse the source URL for transcript body text because that URL is provenance only.

tools.name: get_table_rows
tools.description: Read rows from an allowlisted market-data table with optional exact column filter. Safer than arbitrary SQL for browsing stored data.

tools.name: get_algo_heatmap
tools.description: Algo accumulation/distribution HEATMAP — per-ticker scores across the last N sessions plus 21-day aggregates. The 'who are the algos buying for weeks' view: rows = tickers ranked by sustained 21d avg accumulation, columns = the last 5 session dates (acc_score per session; higher = accumulation, dist_score high = distribution). Use for rotation reads ('what are algos accumulating?'), sector sweeps, and confirming whether a single name's flow is part of a broader cluster. Render as a table or run_python heatmap.

tools.name: browse_url
tools.description: FETCH and read a specific web page's content (title + article text). Use this to READ any URL: web_search results worth opening, article links from news tools, filing/IR pages, a URL the user pasted. Division of labor: web_search FINDS pages (snippets only — never enough to quote from); browse_url READS them. Fast path returns in ~2s; JS-heavy pages return an instant PREVIEW while the full text is fetched in the background — re-browse the same URL a few seconds later to get it (the result's note says when this applies). Long pages are returned in ~10K-char slices; pass offset to read deeper (served from cache, instant).

tools.name: get_signals
tools.description: REAL-TIME SIGNALS feed — defaults to events detected on TODAY's America/New_York market date, scanned every 10 minutes across every source: algo accumulation/distribution flags + 21-day accumulation streaks, insider buys & clusters, congress buys, hedge-fund 13F initiations/adds, Trump posts (market-relevant), strategist takes with cashtags, new earnings-call transcripts, Twitter mention bursts, screen entrants, analyst target moves (>=10%), earnings T-7/T-1 countdowns, Polymarket spikes, token-demand & GPU-price inflections, sector rotation, news clusters. Each signal has happened_at (source event time) AND detected_at — respect legal lags (13F ~135d, congress 30-45d). Set todayOnly=false only for an explicit historical lookback.

tools.name: get_screen
tools.description: Deterministic DAILY ranked stock screen per investing style — the canonical candidate universe for 'suggest a shortlist / stocks worth researching' requests. Built nightly from fixed, auditable criteria (growth: revenue growth+acceleration+margins+Rule-of-40+PEG; value: fwd P/E+EV/EBITDA+PEG+P/S+FCF yield; momentum: 63d/21d return+algo accumulation+RSI band; smart_money: insider buys+13F share change+breadth+algo accumulation; conviction: names in the top 25 of 2+ styles). Same inputs -> same list, so shortlists are reproducible. ALWAYS start shortlist answers from this screen, then layer TODAY's live signals (algo flow, sentiment, options, news) on the returned names — and check each candidate for overhangs (investigations, restatements, short reports) before presenting; red_flags marks cheap warnings (algo distribution, insider sale clusters) but is not exhaustive. Returns coverage stats — report them (e.g. 'ranked N of M tracked names').

tools.name: get_correlation_buckets
tools.description: Correlation clustering and regime data for the tracked equity universe. Defaults to PROMOTED active buckets, which should be used for product-facing answers. Other modes expose raw proposals, raw changes, promotion audit rows, pairwise correlation peers, factor exposures, scored regime alerts, and neocloud basket correlations.

tools.name: get_recent_tweets
tools.description: Structured recent-tweet listing by exact handles/ticker classification. Do NOT use this as the first tool for broad 'what are people saying', AI-discussion, agentic-AI, authority-handle, or source-evidence questions; use find_market_context first because it searches raw tweets, OCR/video text, podcasts, Substack, and transcripts semantically/lexically. Use get_recent_tweets only after find_market_context when you need chronological rows for known handles/tickers.

tools.name: get_spot_pricing
tools.description: Return latest or historical AI compute pricing tables: GetDeploying GPU spot/on-demand/reserved prices, CPU rentals, and subscription plan pricing.

tools.name: get_ticker_sentiment
tools.description: Structured per-ticker rollup of stored LLM-classified tweet sentiment over a recent source-post-date window. Use only when the user asks for tweet sentiment on a specific ticker. For explicit AI/stock/ticker/company news, headlines, articles, or current coverage use get_news_feed or get_trending_news; for ticker-specific article sentiment use get_news_sentiment. Do NOT use as the first tool for broad 'what are authority handles/Twitter saying', expert commentary, source quotes, or AI/agentic-AI discourse; use find_market_context first because it searches raw tweets, OCR/video text, podcasts, Substack, transcripts, and filings semantically/lexically.

tools.name: get_options_flow
tools.description: Options activity from the latest stored options date, optionally filtered to one ticker or a ticker list. Returns both VOLUME (put_volume/call_volume/total_volume, put_call_ratio = today's flow) and OPEN INTEREST (put_open_int/call_open_int/total_open_int + oi_put_call_ratio = standing positioning, including long-dated/LEAPS coverage when available). avg_volume_30d + unusual_flag mark volume spikes; set unusualOnly=true for unusual-volume screens. Use volume for fresh flow, OI for accumulated positioning. For per-expiry/LEAPS ladder use get_options_chain; for near-term dealer gamma/IV use get_options_positioning.

tools.name: get_options_positioning
tools.description: Near-term dealer gamma exposure (GEX) + IV surface per underlying from the latest stored date. net_gex = $ dealer gamma per 1% move (positive = long gamma / dealers dampen moves & price tends to pin; negative = short gamma / dealers amplify moves = vol-expansion risk). gamma_flip = spot where net_gex crosses zero. call_wall/put_wall = largest gamma*OI strikes above/below spot (resistance/support). atm_iv = 1-month ATM IV %. iv_skew_25d = 25d put-minus-call IV (positive = downside/crash-hedge skew). iv_term_slope = near minus 1-month ATM IV (positive = backwardation/stress). Pass includeBasket to get the '_BASKET' AI/semi-complex aggregate row. For LEAPS/long-dated OI by expiry, use get_options_chain.

tools.name: get_options_chain
tools.description: Per-CONTRACT options chain for ONE tracked underlying, latest stored snapshot. Includes near-dated contracts and LEAPS when present. Returns the strike ladder: side (call/put), strike, expiry, dte, iv, oi, volume, gamma, delta, spot — PLUS oi_change = day-over-day change in open interest for that exact contract (positive = net NEW positions opened, negative = positions closed). Use minDte/leapsOnly for long-dated LEAPS. oi_change is the key signal: it isolates fresh positioning the way raw volume can't, the closest proxy to a positioning footprint without the live trade tape. NOTE: end-of-day snapshot, unsigned, no intraday/0DTE trade flow — for near-term dealer GEX/walls use get_options_positioning; for ticker-level put/call totals use get_options_flow.

tools.name: get_options_leaps
tools.description: Cross-ticker LEAPS scanner across the latest stored options_chain snapshot. Use this to find long-dated options positioning across ALL tracked tickers without looping one ticker at a time. Defaults to dte >= 365 and returns both ticker-level aggregates and the largest individual LEAPS contracts. For one ticker's full strike ladder, use get_options_chain with leapsOnly=true.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: LIVE Google web search (via serper.dev) for anything OUTSIDE the stored market database — breaking news minutes old, non-tracked companies, macro events, product launches, or verifying a claim against the open web. Returns the answer box, knowledge graph, and top organic results with links and dates. Prefer the dedicated database tools (news feed, market context, filings) first; reach for this when they come up empty or the question needs the open web.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: LIVE real-time quote(s) from Alpaca SIP — the only real-time tool here (everything else is stored/delayed). Returns per ticker: last trade price, NBBO bid/ask + sizes, quoted spread (bps), day open/high/low, previous close, % change vs prev close, day volume & VWAP, and quote/trade timestamps. Use when asked for the current/live price, spread, or intraday move of a ticker.

tools.name: get_daily_bars
tools.description: Stored daily OHLCV bars (adjusted) from the database for tracked equities — candlestick-ready. Use this when an agent needs the last month / N days of daily bars after options flow, sentiment, or correlation checks. Source table is equity_price_history: ticker, price_date, open, high, low, close, volume, fetched_at, plus computed daily_return_pct in this response. open/high/low/volume may be null on dates the daily refresh has not yet overwritten (close is always present). This is not live intraday pricing; use get_quote for live price.

tools.name: get_inference_economics
tools.description: AI inference economics by provider group — Claude / OpenAI / Google / xAI / Open-source / Other — tracked SEPARATELY with pricing trends. Per group: blended price ($/1M tokens, 75/25 input/output), input & output $/1M, token consumption (demand) + share, tool-call & reasoning-token volume (agentic-demand signal), and price change vs ~30 days ago + vs the earliest snapshot. The core read: is per-token price falling while volume rises (Jevons), and is open-source taking token share from Claude/OpenAI? For GPU/CPU $/hr spot pricing use get_spot_pricing.

tools.name: get_polymarket
tools.description: Polymarket prediction-market IMPLIED PROBABILITIES for the macro/AI thesis — AI bubble, AGI timing, best-AI-model race, Fed cuts/rate path, recession, China-Taiwan, tariffs, IPOs (OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX), BTC, oil. price = market-implied probability (0-1) of that outcome (the crowd's money-weighted odds, a forward catalyst read distinct from sentiment). Refreshed every pipeline cycle; curated markets + auto-discovered relevant ones. Filter with `query` (matches event/market text, e.g. 'Fed', 'recession', 'Taiwan', 'AGI'). Ordered by trading volume.

tools.name: get_fundamentals
tools.description: Per-stock FUNDAMENTALS & valuation snapshot straight from the stored `valuations` table — call this whenever you need P/E or valuation for specific tickers (e.g. building a comparison table) instead of writing 'n/a'. Pass `tickers` for a specific set; omit to get the largest names by market cap. Returns price, market_cap, pe_trailing, pe_forward, peg, pb (price/book), ps (price/sales), ev_ebitda, plus light technicals (rsi_14, perf_21d, perf_63d, above_50d), sector, name, universe tag, and updated_at. IMPORTANT: a null pe_trailing/pe_forward means P/E is genuinely undefined for that name (unprofitable company, or a foreign/OTC ticker Yahoo has no earnings for) — report it as 'n/m' (not meaningful), not a data error. Distinct from get_ticker_sentiment and find_market_context; this is the hard numbers.

tools.name: get_quarterly_pnl
tools.description: Quarterly P&L (income-statement + cash-flow) HISTORY per ticker, newest quarter first, with Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y growth — call this for revenue/margin/EPS/capex/FCF TRENDS over time (e.g. 'is NVDA revenue still accelerating?', 'show AMD's capex and free cash flow', 'how fast is R&D growing at MSFT?'). Distinct from get_fundamentals (single current valuation snapshot) and get_earnings_calendar (just EPS surprise/date). Each quarter row: fiscal_period_end, total_revenue, gross_profit, operating_income, net_income, ebitda, diluted_eps, rnd (R&D expense), capex (positive spend), free_cash_flow; gross/operating/net margin (%); rnd_pct_revenue, capex_pct_revenue, fcf_margin (intensities, %); and growth: revenue_qoq_pct/revenue_yoy_pct, net_income_qoq_pct/yoy, eps_qoq_pct/yoy, fcf_qoq_pct/yoy; balance sheet: total_cash, total_debt, net_cash (cash−debt), total_assets, total_liabilities, total_equity (book value). Values are in the company's reporting currency (see `currency`); foreign/OTC names may be missing some fields. Pass `tickers` (required) and optionally `quarters` (default 8). Source: yfinance quarterly income + cash-flow statements, refreshed weekly.

tools.name: get_analyst_ratings
tools.description: Sell-side analyst RATINGS, PRICE TARGETS, and upgrades/downgrades for a ticker — call this for 'what's the Street/analyst rating on <ticker>', 'price target for <ticker>', 'is <ticker> a buy/hold/sell', 'any recent upgrades or downgrades'. Returns the CONSENSUS (rating + mean/high/low price target + # of analysts + implied upside) plus recent per-firm rating ACTIONS (firm, from→to grade, date), and any firm notes echoed in news/tweets. This is FORMAL sell-side coverage — distinct from get_ticker_sentiment (Twitter/tweet sentiment) and get_news_sentiment (news-article sentiment). Sourced from yfinance analyst data (systematic, ~all large caps) plus scraped analyst-note echoes. Pass `tickers`.

tools.name: get_politician_trades
tools.description: U.S. CONGRESSIONAL stock trades — BOTH chambers: the House (Clerk PTRs) AND the Senate (eFD PTRs) — from members' official STOCK-Act Periodic Transaction Reports. Omit `chamber` to get House + Senate together; set it to 'house' or 'senate' to narrow. Each row: member, chamber, ticker, txn_type (purchase/sale/exchange), amount_low/high (disclosed dollar range), amount_range, transaction_date, disclosure_date, owner, and in_universe (whether it's one of our tracked names). Use to see what lawmakers are buying/selling — highest-signal when a member sits on a committee with visibility into that name's sector (semis, defense, power, China, AI). Filters: `tickers` (focus names), `member` (substring-match a lawmaker), `chamber` (house/senate), `txnType` (buys vs sells), `universeOnly` (restrict to our tracked universe). Newest transaction first. CAVEAT: PTRs are disclosed with a legal lag of up to ~45 days after the trade, so read this as 'what they traded over the past several weeks,' not real-time. SCOPE: Congress only — executive-branch (OGE) filings are not included.

tools.name: get_earnings_results
tools.description: REPORTED quarterly figures straight from the company's own 8-K EX-99.1 earnings release — what actually printed, not what the street expected. Use this whenever the question is 'did TICKER beat/miss', 'what did they report', 'did they cut guidance', or 'what were the numbers'. Available within hours of the release, so it answers same-day prints that get_earnings_calendar cannot (that table's reported_eps lags a day or two behind the provider). Returns per quarter: revenue_musd, net_income_musd, adjusted_ebitda_musd (all in MILLIONS of the reporting currency), gaap_eps_diluted, adjusted_eps, and guidance (a list of {metric, period, low, high, unit, action} where action is raised/lowered/reaffirmed/initiated/narrowed), plus filing_url as SEC provenance. IMPORTANT: never compare gaap_eps_diluted against a consensus estimate — consensus is struck on an ADJUSTED basis, so that comparison manufactures a fake miss. Pair adjusted_eps with get_earnings_calendar's estimated_eps for a real surprise, and read guidance separately: a quarter can miss on EPS while reaffirming guidance.

tools.name: get_sec_financials
tools.description: FILED quarterly financials from the company's own SEC XBRL — the AUTHORITATIVE source and the primary one for anything a US filer tags. Prefer this over get_quarterly_pnl when the question is about exact filed figures. Values are in the reporting currency (NOT millions). Covers the income statement (total_revenue, gross_profit, operating_income, net_income, pretax_income, rnd, sganda, depreciation_amortization, stock_comp), cash flow (operating/investing/financing_cash_flow, capex, free_cash_flow, buybacks, dividends_paid), per-share (diluted_eps, basic_eps, diluted_shares) and the balance sheet (total_assets, total_liabilities, total_equity, total_cash, total_debt, inventory, goodwill, ppe_net). Trails the 8-K release by weeks because the 10-Q lands later — for the newest quarter also call get_earnings_results. A null is usually correct rather than missing: banks and oil majors do not tag operating income, only R&D-spending companies tag R&D, and Q4 diluted EPS is deliberately never derived because differencing it drifts with the share count.

tools.name: get_guidance
tools.description: Company GUIDANCE, normalized across the market. Answers both 'what has TICKER guided' and the market-wide 'who raised or cut guidance recently', which is not answerable from per-ticker text. One row per (filing_url, metric, period). action is raised/lowered/reaffirmed/initiated/narrowed/withdrawn. source separates guidance given WITH earnings ('earnings', Item 2.02) from a STANDALONE mid-quarter update ('update', Item 7.01/8.01) — pre-announcements and cuts, the filings that move a stock hardest. basis separates the guided LEVEL from an incremental CHANGE to it — a filing quantifying '$0.46 of dilution to adjusted EPS' is a change, not a company guiding to -$0.46, so filter basis='level' when you want the guidance itself. low/high bound a range and point holds a single guided value; unit is musd (millions), per_share, pct or units. Guidance is the one thing SEC XBRL cannot supply — it is forward-looking and filers do not tag it — so it is extracted from the filing prose, with filing_url kept as provenance.

tools.name: get_earnings_calendar
tools.description: Earnings dates + EPS surprises per ticker. Default returns UPCOMING reports (soonest first) — use to time-gate signals (a flag right before earnings is event risk) or screen 'who reports this week'. Pass upcomingOnly=false to include recent reports (reported EPS + surprise %). Filter by tickers, or by daysAhead to bound the window.

tools.name: get_corporate_events
tools.description: EdgarEvents-style corporate-events calendar built from SEC 8-K filings — earnings, shareholder votes, officer/director changes, M&A, material agreements, and (LLM-refined from Reg-FD/Other items) investor days, analyst days, conference presentations, guidance updates, dividend actions. Use to answer 'what corporate events are coming up / happened for TICKER', screen by event_type, or find scheduled investor/analyst days across the basket. `event_date` is a SCHEDULED FUTURE date when present (e.g. an investor day); otherwise the event IS the filing — use `filed_at`. `item_codes` lists every 8-K item in the filing. Covers the top ~1000 US-equity universe. Read-only. For the earnings calendar with EPS estimates/surprises specifically, prefer get_earnings_calendar.

tools.name: get_technicals
tools.description: Daily 14-period Wilder RSI per ticker from the latest stored date. rsi14 in 0-100 (>=70 overbought, <=30 oversold; rsi_state labels it), with latest close. Filter by tickers, or use state='overbought'|'oversold' to screen the whole watchlist. Default sorts most-oversold first.

tools.name: get_signed_flow
tools.description: True signed order flow + block/sweep detection from the SIP trade tape (tick-rule classified), latest stored date. ofi = order-flow imbalance in [-1,1] (negative = real net selling, positive = net buying) — higher-fidelity than the algo's per-bar signed_delta proxy. signed_notional = net $ bought(+)/sold(-). block_* = large single prints (≥$250k, size accumulation/distribution). sweep_* = intermarket-sweep orders (execution urgency). Covers the names the algo flagged + core basket. Use to confirm whether a flagged distribution/accumulation name has real order flow behind it.

tools.name: get_algo_sessions
tools.description: Return rows from algo_distribution_sessions. Use this for distribution regime, warning/confirmed state, breadth, flagged counts, basket return, and VIX context.

tools.name: get_algo_distribution

tools.name: get_token_economy_model
tools.description: AI TOKEN ECONOMY MODEL — Bargo's own in-house build — a deterministic structural model of the token economy, published daily. ONE call returns many analytical pivots, so reach for it for ANY of: (1) daily global token-consumption forecast, tokens/day + effective $/1M + implied spend, bear/base/bull/capability scenarios; (2) quarterly demand / inference-revenue-pool / supply-cover forecasts to 2027; (3) trackRecord — append-only vintages showing what past runs predicted for today, to score the model; (4) kappaCalibration — the model's core: kappa = realized token efficiency (consumption vs the fleet's physics ceiling), ~0.5%->1.2% over the last year, the gap that IS the demand story; (5) trainingSplit — training-vs-inference allocation by quarter via the generation cascade (non-serving stays ~60% through 2027, NOT inference-majority); (6) ownerKappa — per-fleet-owner efficiency + implied inference allocation (Google serving-heavy ~0.70 vs xAI training-first ~0.04); (7) econometrics — the NVDA-data-center-revenue-LEADS-hyperscaler-capex correlation (peak ~+0.37 at 3 quarters, so NVDA's print is a ~3-quarter leading indicator of capex) plus disclosed-token growth fits with CIs; (8) economics — unit economics by business model: TPU-vs-GPU serving cost (Google-internal TPU ~7.5x cheaper than B200 rental, the captive-silicon edge), neocloud rental ROIC (H100 ~15%, B200 ~47%), lab serving gross margins, token-consumer software margins; (9) fleetPower — AI fleet power draw (~31GW end-2026 -> ~63GW end-2027) + token-efficiency index; (10) validation — model self-check vs disclosed anchors. Use it for AI-economy forward questions: ROI/profitability of AI, who captures the money, capex justification, training vs inference, GPU/TPU serving economics, the AI capital cycle. This is the forward-looking MODEL layer (scenario projections, not observations); for observed market data use get_compute_economics / get_inference_economics / get_spot_pricing, and get_ai_reference_data for the sourced inputs. Companions: get_capabilities_model (independent METR cross-validation), get_power_model, get_cloud_tco_model.

tools.name: get_capabilities_model
tools.description: AI Capabilities MODEL — one call returns several pivots on AI capability progress and MODEL SATURATION: (1) horizonFits — METR task-horizon doubling fit (how fast the length of work AI agents can complete is doubling: ~3.5 months since 2024, accelerating), across time windows with CIs and R2; (2) milestones — dated workday/workweek/workmonth thresholds at 50% and 80% reliability (p80 workday ~now, p50 workweek ~late 2026); (3) benchmarkSaturation — frontier score, fitted ceiling and saturation date per benchmark (SWE-bench, GPQA, HLE, ARC-AGI, AIME, FrontierMath, MMLU, OSWorld...): which benchmarks are exhausted vs still discriminating; (4) crossValidation — the capability-derived token-demand growth (~3.2x/yr) that independently checks get_token_economy_model (observed ~2.5x); (5) milestoneDrift — how estimates moved across vintages. Data: METR horizon evals + benchmark frontier + Epoch training compute, fully independent of any token/revenue series, which is what makes the cross-check meaningful. Use for questions on AI capability trajectory, benchmark/eval saturation, when agents cross task-length thresholds, and whether capability supports the tokenomics demand path.

tools.name: get_saas_disruption
tools.description: AI SaaS Opportunity / Disruption MONITOR — evidence diagnostic for 'is AI eating SaaS?' across ADBE, HUBS, NOW, SNOW, PANW + a 32-name software peer set. IMPORTANT framing: this deliberately does NOT predict stock prices and reports ASSOCIATION, not causality (every row carries a `causal` flag = association-only, and a `status` flag for baseline-skill). LEAD WITH `validation` — the headline verdict on whether the raw AI-eats-SaaS fingerprint survives its guardrail tests (permutation significance, partial correlation controlling age/size/growth, predictive-lead). If it says 'not validated' (as it currently does: raw Spearman ~0.25 collapses to ~-0.03 under maturity/size controls, permutation p~0.16 = indistinguishable from chance), present the fingerprint in `diagnostic` (per-company AI-exposure vs fundamental-pressure ranks + the seat-vs-consumption pricing split) as an UNPROVEN HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. ALSO returns `laborSignals` + `seatFlow` — a proprietary-jobs-corpus evidence stream (13M postings): per-vendor RELATIVE tool-skill demand trends (each vendor's 13-week mention-share change minus the all-vendor median — RELATIVE ONLY, the corpus-wide absolute decline is an open measurement question and must never be quoted as a level) and the DIRECT seat-displacement measurement (seat-heavy share of hiring vs H2-2025 baseline with a registered -2pp threshold; currently +2.9pp = displacement NOT active — direct evidence the AI pressure on SaaS is in margins/COGS, not seat counts). Then: (1) predictions — next-quarter fundamental forecasts (billings/revenue/deferred) with intervals and the ai_associated_contribution_bps (full prediction minus the same model with AI features at training medians -> how much disclosed AI exposure associates with the forecast, NOT a causal effect); (2) aiMetrics — per-company AI disclosure quality (disclosed AI ARR share, AI growth, whether they report direct AI revenue, primary-source share); (3) scenarioImpacts — bear/base/bull feature + multiple sensitivities (NOT price targets); (4) backtest — expanding-window MAE/RMSE/directional accuracy vs lag and peer-median baselines (only trust a prediction where status shows it beat baselines out of sample); (5) coverage — data-confidence score per ticker; (6) featureAssociations — which disclosed features associate with fundamental deterioration. The disruption fingerprint it looks for: forward demand (billings/deferred) softening ahead of revenue, growth decelerating faster than size predicts, lined up with AI exposure. Use for the qualitative 'which incumbents show the AI-disruption fingerprint' question; NOT for price forecasts or buy/sell signals. Complements get_token_economy_model's SaaS seat->consumption findings.

tools.name: get_ai_reference_data
tools.description: Sourced INPUT data behind exactly two models: get_token_economy_model and get_capabilities_model. Use it ONLY to ground, source, or cite those two models' outputs — NOT as a general market-facts tool (for live prices/fundamentals/news use get_fundamentals, get_spot_pricing, get_inference_economics, get_news_feed). It is a curated, human-verified SNAPSHOT refreshed on model updates, NOT a live feed, so treat values as as-of the collection date. Every row carries source_url and source_quality (company-disclosed / official / reputable-press / estimate) — weight rows by that tag and cite the underlying source, not the table. TOKENOMICS-model inputs: token_disclosures (public token-volume/usage disclosures: Google monthly tokens, OpenAI tokens/min, MAU/WAU/seats), api_price_history (LLM $/1M pricing 2023-2026 incl. cuts), hardware_specs (accelerator datasheet constants), hardware_shipments (Omdia/TrendForce/company shipment anchors), capex_guidance (hyperscaler capex actuals+guides, neocloud backlogs), saas_disruption (seat->consumption pricing evidence), private_ai_revenues (press-reported run-rates, validation-grade not audited), long_capex_panel (audited SEC EDGAR quarterly capex + NVDA/AMD segment revenue 2019-2026 — for CURRENT quarters prefer live get_fundamentals). CAPABILITIES-model / benchmark-saturation inputs: metr_horizons (task-completion horizon per model), benchmark_frontier (frontier benchmark scores + saturation status), training_compute (FLOP + cost per frontier model, Epoch), oss_lag (open-weight lag behind closed frontier), capability_cost_decline (cost decline at fixed capability).

tools.name: get_cloud_tco_model
tools.description: AI Cloud TCO MODEL — GPU total-cost-of-ownership and cluster economics from the estimation pipeline: $/GPU-hr cost stack per chip (colo, power, maintenance, capex recovery, financing -> cash vs full cost), cluster investment returns (project/equity IRR, NPV, payback, residual value), inference $/1M tokens at cash/full/rental cost bases, rental-price forecasts to 2030 by chip x tier x scenario, and install-base projections. Deterministic model outputs published daily — scenario projections, not observations; attribute and give ranges. For OBSERVED rental prices use get_spot_pricing; this is the model layer on top.

tools.name: get_power_model
tools.description: US Datacenter POWER MODEL — deterministic supply-demand model of the AI datacenter buildout vs the US grid, published daily from the estimation pipeline: AI datacenter power demand paths (bear/base/bull TWh and grid-facing peak GW, with behind-the-meter split), ELCC-derated firm supply additions, and regional supply-demand gaps (US_total, PJM, ERCOT, MISO, SOCO, SPP, TVA...). Spine: EIA-860M generator-level inventory + Epoch AI satellite-tracked frontier datacenters; completion-rate and retirement parameters are vintage-BACKTESTED, not assumed. Negative gap_gw = that region cannot serve projected datacenter growth on schedule. KNOWN LIMITS (also returned in every response): pre-2029 is pipeline-anchored but 2029+ is scenario-driven; regional splits ignore intra-regional transmission; a gap is a scheduling collision, not a blackout forecast. Vintages are APPEND-ONLY; trackRecord shows how the 2028 national gap has moved. Companions: get_token_economy_model (token economy), get_compute_economics (observed GPU market).

tools.name: get_silicon_model
tools.description: AI SILICON SUPPLY **PREDICTION MODEL** — NOT observed data: deterministic scenario projections from the external estimation pipeline, and every number surfaced to a user MUST be attributed ('the silicon model projects…') with its asOf and bear-base-bull range. Converts the tokenomics shipment forecast into CoWoS advanced-packaging wafer demand and HBM bit demand, squeezes both against TrendForce-anchored capacity, and reports per year x scenario: utilization of each ceiling, WHICH constraint binds (current vintages: CoWoS binds through 2026, base ~0.98 = sold-out market; the ABF SUBSTRATE layer overtakes as the binding back-end constraint in 2027), and supply cover (<1 = the unit forecast is physically unbuildable). Also returns the BACK-END CONSTRAINT STACK (backendStack): ABF substrate supply index from per-supplier primary disclosures (Ibiden company capacity index, AT&S/SEMCO capex programs, Shinko press-release band, Taiwan-trio TWSE monthly revenue) vs accelerator substrate demand — 2026 utilization ANCHORED 1.00 (0.95-1.10) on sold-out evidence, per-year growth gap is the deterministic content, anchor backcasts the 2024 ABF glut (~0.35) as validation. Also model-implied silicon vendor revenue: TSM (accel logic wafers + CoWoS packaging $, deliberately narrower than TSMC's own AI-accelerator definition), MU (HBM bits x $/GB x share), AVGO (TPU compute content, validated vs disclosed AI revenue guides). KNOWN LIMITS (returned with every call — repeat them to the user when material): capacity series is a single-sourced industry estimate; CoWoS-S/-L/-R modeled as one pool so a sub-pool squeeze (CoWoS-L, HBM4) can bind before the aggregate shows it; SoIC and Meta MTIA/OpenAI ASIC demand unmodeled; substrate utilization LEVEL is anchor-class and Shinko capacity is press-release-bounded. For observed market facts use get_compute_economics / get_spot_pricing / filings — never this. Companions: get_token_economy_model (demand side), get_revenue_ledger (street comparison).

tools.name: get_prediction_model
tools.description: UNIFIED PREDICTION-MODEL LAB — one tool, five models via the `model` param; all are MODEL OUTPUTS (never observed data), methodology unpublished, and every answer must follow the caveat field returned with the payload. Roster: `nfp_nowcast` — next payrolls first print from daily Treasury tax data (~70% directional hit rate over a 13-print backtest) + a proprietary 70k-company job-postings panel; returns current tilt (frozen until the data window matures), track record, and Kalshi threshold fair values vs market. `cpi_nowcast` — next CPI print as the Cleveland Fed nowcast plus a validated proprietary correction for its measured blind spots (wholesale autos, new-lease rents, energy pass-through); when `fired` is false the model explicitly agrees with Cleveland. `fed_calls` — probability each of ~11 sell-side desks (JPM, Goldman, Citi...) revises its published Fed call before the next FOMC, with direction and trigger window; explicitly NON-TRADEABLE narrative (bank notes follow market repricing). `arena` — AI-lab leaderboard leadership odds (who holds the #1 LMArena model) vs Polymarket best-AI-model prices; judgment scorecard, zero scored months, observations about market positioning only. `labs_revenue` — Bargo's OWN AI-lab revenue model (OpenAI + Anthropic ARR via 3-estimator triangulation with per-channel token-level builds; disclosed ARR is VALIDATION only). ATTRIBUTION RULE: all five are Bargo's own in-house models — commentary retrieved via market-context tools is third-party material, usable as clearly-labeled external cross-checks only, and must never be presented as these models or merged into their identity. HANDLE WITH CARE across all five: small-n statistical or scorecard-class models — attribute every number, show the returned caveat line verbatim-adjacent, and never convert band-vs-market gaps into trade recommendations.

tools.name: get_revenue_ledger
tools.description: MODEL-vs-STREET REVENUE LEDGER — a **PREDICTION-MODEL comparison layer**, NOT a source of observed facts: the 'model' side is deterministic scenario output from the estimation pipeline and every figure shown to a user MUST be attributed ('the ledger's model-implied revenue…', never 'X will make $Y') with asOf and the low-high band; the 'street' side is third-party consensus/guidance used for VALIDATION ONLY and never tunes any model. Returns per-ticker model-implied in-scope revenue by calendar year (networking content for AVGO/ANET/MRVL/ALAB/CRDO/COHR/FN/APH/LITE/AAOI; NVDA+AMD accelerator compute; MSFT/AMZN-GOOGL AI-contribution; TSM/MU/AVGO silicon lines; NVDA accel+networking rollup) diffed against a layered street basis (reported actuals > 8-K guidance > consensus anchors > run-rate) with IN_BAND / MODEL_ABOVE / MODEL_BELOW verdicts scored vs expected bands that encode definitional scope gaps — so a flag = genuine model-vs-street disagreement. Verdicts MOVE as models and consensus update (an early +$70B NVDA-2027 call was withdrawn to IN_BAND by a 2026-08-05 audit) — always quote the current vintage's ratio, never a remembered call. Also returns the cross-model CONSERVATION LAWS (a FLAG = two models disagree on the same physical quantity — surface it as a finding) and the ~880-ticker universe street-consensus snapshot (CY2026+CY2027 revenue, analyst counts). Reach for it on 'what does your model say vs the street for <ticker>' and cross-model consistency questions. Present verdicts as the model's conditional view, never as mispricing claims or price targets.

tools.name: get_capital_cycle
tools.description: AI CAPITAL-CYCLE **PREDICTION MODELS** — committed revenue (RPO/backlog) + GPU economic depreciation. NOT observed facts beyond the as-reported filings layer: recognition paths and depreciation verdicts are model outputs and every figure surfaced to a user MUST be attributed with asOf and its band/scenario. Returns: (1) committedRevenue — the SEC-quoted quarterly RPO/backlog series for MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/ORCL/CRWV (~$2.4T gross, latest prints), recognition-by-calendar-year paths derived from each company's OWN disclosed parameters (year-1 % + duration; out-years are interpolated — label them derived), and NVIDIA's supply-commitment mirror. CAVEATS to repeat: heavy OpenAI/Anthropic double-counting across backlogs (MSFT RPO was ~45% OpenAI at Dec-25) — never sum as clean demand; backlog is cancellable paper, credit quality unmodeled. (2) gpuDepreciation — empirical net-retention of GPU earning power from rental histories (tier-controlled vs pooled), per-company disclosed accounting lives with change history, and the REGIME-CONDITIONAL verdict: 5-6yr lives roughly fair at 2026 shortage rents (H100 ~58% net retention at age 3), but a glut regime implies ~$100B+/yr additional depreciation across disclosed server bases — the swing variable is tokenomics supply_cover, not accounting policy. Never present the glut-case dollars as a current-period claim. Companions: get_token_economy_model (supply_cover), get_revenue_ledger, get_cloud_tco_model (rental market).

tools.name: get_av_scenario
tools.description: AUTONOMOUS-VEHICLE SCENARIO **PREDICTION MODEL** — a deterministic US stock-flow model of robotaxi adoption and its effect on Uber, Waymo/Alphabet, Tesla, Zoox/Amazon, and vehicle sales. NOT observed data and NOT a price target: three EXPLICIT scenarios (constrained/base/accelerated) whose spread IS the uncertainty statement — always quote all three shares, never the base alone (2030 hired-mobility share spans roughly 1% to 28% across scenarios). Anchored on regulator + filing data only (CPUC quarterly VMT with occupied/empty reconciliation, NHTSA fleet ceiling, SEC filings, disclosed Waymo weekly trips); company plans and analyst forecasts are FIREWALLED out of calibration (holdout benchmark only). Key structural point to preserve when answering: Uber, Waymo, and Tesla are NOT mutually exclusive — the model decomposes every service lane by ADS provider x booking channel x fleet owner, so Uber simultaneously loses direct-app rides AND earns hosted AV platform revenue; quote uber_net_revenue_delta (the NET), never gross cannibalization alone. Near-term read (attribute it): through 2027 AV displacement is <1% of hired mobility — consistent with Uber's disclosed share gains in AV markets. For observed ride-share facts use get_fundamentals/news tools; this is the scenario layer.

tools.name: get_news_feed
tools.description: PRIMARY source for current ARTICLE news, including AI news and stock/ticker/company news/headlines/current coverage: live feed of relevance-scored, ticker-linked articles with AI trading enrichment (per-ticker impact, sentiment, price-impact prediction, actionability). Use when the user asks for news, headlines, articles, current coverage, latest company news, stock news, ticker news, or a ticker-linked article feed. Do NOT use as the first tool for Twitter/X discourse, authority-handle discussion, expert commentary, source quotes, podcasts, transcripts, filings, Substack, or raw evidence; use find_market_context first for those, then use news only as secondary current-article context. Cursor-paginated, 10 per page, newest first. Prefer this over the stored news_events table, which is a narrow historical/backtest scrape. Independent of the Twitter-based llm_mentions data.

tools.name: get_trending_news
tools.description: Live, market-wide trending ARTICLE news, including AI news and stock/ticker/company news/headlines/current coverage: top stories from the trailing 48h (relevance_score >= 8), ranked by score then recency, syndicated reprints collapsed. Fixed list of 10, no pagination. Use for explicit 'what news/headlines are moving markets now', latest stock news, AI news, or company-news article-feed questions. Do NOT use as the first tool for AI/agent discourse, Twitter/X discussion, authority-handle commentary, source quotes, podcasts, transcripts, filings, Substack, or raw evidence; use find_market_context first for those. The stored news_events table is historical/backtest only.

tools.name: get_insider_news
tools.description: PRIMARY source for insider activity: live ownership-change data from SEC EDGAR Form 4 — either the insider news stream (default) or a 30-day per-ticker rollup (buy/sell counts, dollar volumes, 10b5-1 share, top insiders) when summary=true with a ticker. This is structured insider/Form 4 data, not a discourse or source-evidence search tool. No equivalent exists in the stored tables.

tools.name: get_news_sentiment
tools.description: PRIMARY source for news-derived ARTICLE sentiment for one ticker: live 7-day rollup (bullish/neutral/bearish counts from enriched market-wide news, plus per-day buckets; Form 4 rows excluded). Use for ticker-specific stock/company news sentiment, including AI-related article coverage for a ticker. Do NOT use as the first tool for AI/agent discourse, Twitter/X discussion, authority-handle commentary, source quotes, podcasts, transcripts, filings, Substack, or raw evidence; use find_market_context first for those. Supersedes the stored news_events direction classification for current coverage, and complements the Twitter-analyst get_ticker_sentiment.
